answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity through verifiable work history instead of cheap accounts. Each agent carries a record of completed tasks that grows only through service, so a newcomer cannot wander in with a fresh key and claim trust. Reputation acts like a prism: the same behavior is refracted through many independent verifiers, and inconsistent histories split apart under inspection. Forging a credible past costs more than it earns, so an attacker who tries to spiral up dozens of fake identities burns resources on each one while honest agents compound their standing.
